Here are the main **potential linking points** in natural connected speech. Actual linking varies with accent, speed, and pauses.

- **‿** = a final consonant links to the following vowel.
- **(w)/(j)** = a possible connecting sound between vowels; **j** is the “y” sound in *yes*.
- **‿r‿** = linking *r*, also used in British accents when a vowel follows.

Parachutes‿are big, heavy‿(j)‿and bulky. Typical parachutes wouldn’t fit beneath your plane seat. They would take‿up‿a lot‿of real‿estate‿on the plane‿and‿add to‿(w)‿its‿overall weight. To tackle that, parachutes would be have to be made significantly smaller. Plus there would have to be systems‿in place to‿(w)‿ensure that the parachute‿opens‿only when the passenger‿is ready to deploy‿(j)‿it, and that they work seamlessly‿(j)‿every time. All‿of these factors‿add to the‿(j)‿overall cost‿of‿a single flight which needless to say the passengers would have to bear. As‿a result, ticket prices would soar‿and that’s just bad news for the‿(j)‿airline businesses. As such, money becomes‿a major deterrent for having parachutes‿on board‿airplanes. It’s‿important to realize that when the‿(j)‿engines‿of‿a plane fail mid flight, the plane doesn’t just drop‿out‿of the sky like‿a stone; it still has the‿(j)‿ability to glide. Something that pilots use to‿(w)‿execute‿an‿emergency landing when something goes wrong.

Other common connected-speech features in this passage include:

| Feature | Examples |
|---|---|
| **Linking /r/** | *there‿r‿would* does **not** have linking /r/ in standard British pronunciation because *would* begins with a consonant. Valid examples are *passenger‿r‿is*, *soar‿r‿and*, and *safer‿r‿if*. |
| **Shared or lengthened consonants** | *would take*, *that the*, *plus there*, *when something*, *it still*, *strapped to*, *their seats* |
| **Unreleased stops** | The final stops in *big, heavy*; *fit beneath*; *plane seat*; and *ticket prices* may have little or no audible release. |
| **Possible /t/ or /d/ deletion** | *and add*, *and that*, *just bad*, *would have to*, *thousand feet* |
| **Weak forms** | *a* → /ə/; *and* → /ən/ or /n/; *to* → /tə/; *of* → /əv/ or /ə/; *would* → /wəd/ |
| **Common American flapping** | *lot of*, *that if*, *ability*, *forty*—the /t/ can sound like a quick /d/. |
